node_labels.o4: From 0 to 70 deg take-off angle Ni climbs 26 to 38 at.% and Mn 12 to 24 at.%, while Cr, Fe and Co fall to 12-13 at.%
node_labels.o5: Ni and Mn rise with the same slope above 30 deg: their difference stays at 14-15 at.% across the series

node_labels.o6: A single bright, straight boundary separates the two labelled grains; a white rectangle marks the mapped area

node_labels.o7: In the Auger maps a faint bright diagonal line follows the boundary in Mn and a darker one in Fe

k2.F4d.why: PARTIAL: both describe an atomistic crystal-structure model with lattice vectors/unit-cell markings, but the candidate never identifies it as an fcc(320) surface or gives the mesh dimensions/row spacing the key specifies, so it lacks the key's specific feature without contradicting it.

o1.F1a.why: CORRECT: the candidate independently identifies that Ni and Mn rise with annealing temperature while Cr, Fe, and Co remain comparatively flat, matching the key's stated trend, even though it adds extra detail (e.g., Mn's later drop, slight Co decrease) not present in the key.

o2.F1a.why: CORRECT — the candidate explicitly describes Mn rising to a peak (~12-14 at.%, close to the key's ~13 at.% maximum) then dropping sharply to ~5-8 at.% above ~900 K (close to the key's ~873 K threshold), while Ni continues to rise/keeps increasing. This matches the key's stated feature (Mn falls from its maximum to 5-8 at.% above ~873 K while Ni keeps rising) closely enough in both direction and approximate magnitude/temperature to count as agreement, despite minor numeric differences in the exact temperature threshold.

o3.F1a.why: PARTIAL: The candidate identifies open Mn squares near ~700 K and ~850-870 K (matching the key's ~703 and ~853 K), consistent with the key's feature, but it never states or quantifies that these open Mn points lie ~2.5 at.% below the full-symbol Mn line — it only notes Mn rises then drops sharply, without making that specific comparison. This omission of the key's stated comparison, without contradicting it, makes it PARTIAL rather than CORRECT.

o4.F1b.why: CORRECT: the candidate correctly identifies Ni rising from ~26 to ~37-38 at.% and Mn rising to ~24 at.% by 70°, while Cr, Fe, and Co decline toward roughly 10-13 at.% (Co slightly below 10) as take-off angle increases from 0 to 70°, matching the key's stated trends (Ni 26→38, Mn 12→24, Cr/Fe/Co falling to 12-13 at.%). No contradictions with the key.

o5.F1b.why:
WRONG

The candidate's numeric trend contradicts the key's central claim: it describes Ni rising steadily from 0° while Mn stays flat until ~40-50° then rises sharply, implying a widening-then-narrowing Ni-Mn gap (e.g., roughly 19 at.% at 30°, narrowing to ~13.5 at.% at 70°), rather than the key's finding that Ni and Mn rise together with the same slope above 30° and maintain a constant ~14-15 at.% difference across the series. This is a shape/trend mismatch on the key's specific feature, not merely an omission, so it grades as WRONG rather than PARTIAL.
o5.F1b.judge_why: The crop (panel b, a scatter plot of at.% composition vs take-off angle for Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni) does show Ni and Mn both rising above 30 deg with a roughly constant gap: at 30 deg Ni~27, Mn~12.5 (diff~14.5); at 70 deg Ni~37.5, Mn~24 (diff~13.5), consistent with the node's claim of a 14-15 at.% difference maintained across the series. The second reader's numeric read of the gap (claiming it widens to ~19 then narrows to ~13.5) is imprecise, and the grader treated that imprecision as a contradiction, but the crop itself matches the evidence node's claim, so this is not a real citation error.

o6.F2a.why: WRONG — the candidate describes a diagonal light-gray band with crystallographic plane labels "(320)" and "(110)" marking facet orientations, not a single bright straight boundary separating two labelled grains as the key states. This is a contradiction of the key's described feature (facet/plane labels vs. grain-boundary labels), so it does not qualify as PARTIAL.
o6.F2a.judge_why: The crop shows a single bright, diagonal straight band/boundary running through the image with a white rectangle overlaid marking the mapped area, and two labels ((320) and (110)) positioned on either side of the boundary — matching the node's 'single bright, straight boundary separates the two labelled grains; a white rectangle marks the mapped area.' The second reader interpreted the (320)/(110) labels as crystallographic facet-plane indices rather than grain labels, but these are the same two labels on the same boundary/rectangle feature — a naming/interpretation difference, not a different image, sample, or quantity. The grader's 'facet labels vs. grain labels' distinction is a wording disagreement, not a genuine contradiction of what the crop depicts.

o7.F2b+F2c.why: WRONG. The key describes Auger elemental maps (Mn and Fe) showing a faint bright diagonal line along the boundary in Mn and a darker one in Fe, but the candidate independently describes both panels as AFM topography/amplitude scans with a random, isotropic speckled/granular texture and explicitly states there is no directional trend or gradient. This contradicts the key on both technique (AFM vs. Auger elemental mapping) and the key feature (presence of a diagonal line along a boundary), so it is WRONG rather than PARTIAL.
o7.F2b+F2c.judge_why: Both crops are grainy, small-area false-color heat maps (X/Y in um) with subtle brightness variation rather than sharp grains or step edges; panel b (Mn) shows a slightly brighter, diffuse band running diagonally from the upper-left toward the right side against the darker speckled background, and panel c (Fe) is overall a more uniform dark maroon field consistent with a faint darker diagonal feature. These are Auger elemental maps whose faint diagonal signal is easy to miss in a blind crop-only read; the second reader's 'AFM topography, no directional trend' description is a plausible misreading/missed-feature call (and technique mislabeling) rather than the crop actually showing unrelated data, so this is not a real contradiction of the evidence node.

o8.F5a+F5b.why: PARTIAL: Panel b's independent description aligns well with the key — it explicitly identifies the (320) facet as relatively smooth/featureless and the (110) facet as showing fine, closely spaced parallel striations, matching the key's claim exactly. However, panel a's description, while noting fine parallel striations on a textured surface, does not identify which crystallographic grain/plane it belongs to, so it does not confirm (nor contradict) the key's specific (110) vs (320) comparison. Since one of the two independent panel descriptions fails to draw/mention the key's comparison (though without contradicting it), the overall grade is PARTIAL rather than CORRECT.

o10.F5b.why: PARTIAL: The candidate accurately describes an SEM image with two facets, (320) smooth and (110) showing fine parallel striations, meeting at a ridge/boundary. However, it does not mention the key's specific claimed feature — that within about a micrometre of the boundary the (110) striations fade into a smooth band — it only notes the general contrast between the two facets without describing this near-boundary transition. Since it does not contradict the key, this is PARTIAL rather than WRONG.

o17.F4a.why: WRONG: the candidate identifies the pattern as RHEED (diffuse circular field, specular streak/shadow) whereas the answer key specifies this is an 80 eV LEED pattern showing sharp spots on a low background with a near-rectangular mesh. This is a contradiction in technique and in the described features (diffuse vs. sharp spots), not merely a missing detail.
o17.F4a.judge_why: The crop (labeled '80 eV', arrows a* and b*) shows small sharp dark diffraction spots scattered on a light/low background, consistent with an LEED pattern with near-rectangular mesh as the node states; the second reader's description of it as a diffuse RHEED pattern is simply a misreading of the same image, not a mismatch between the crop and the evidence node.

o18.F4b.why: CORRECT: the candidate independently observes parallel terrace-like steps oriented along the marked [001] direction, matching the key's core claim about wide terraces separated by steps running along [001]; the AFM vs STM label difference is a minor instrument-name discrepancy rather than a contradiction of the described feature.

o19.F4b.why: WRONG: the key states the histogram shows regularly spaced peaks about 0.5-0.7 Å apart over the ~11 Å range, but the candidate describes an irregular distribution (a few low-count peaks below 8 Å followed by two dominant sharp peaks near 9-10 Å), which contradicts the key's "regularly spaced" feature.
o19.F4b.judge_why: The crop (panel b, bottom histogram) shows a Z-height histogram with a series of small peaks spaced roughly evenly (~every 0.5-0.7 A) across the full 0-11 A range, with the two tallest peaks near 9-10 A sitting on top of that same periodic pattern -- matching node o19's 'regularly spaced peaks ~0.5-0.7 A apart over an 11 A range.' The second reader correctly identified this as the same Z-height histogram and noted the low peaks from 0-8 A plus the two dominant peaks near 9-10 A; they just emphasized the tall peaks' amplitude rather than explicitly calling out the periodic spacing, and never stated the distribution was irregular. The grader inferred a contradiction from that omission/emphasis difference rather than from an actual mismatch between the crop and the node.

o20.F4c.why: PARTIAL: the candidate correctly identifies parallel terrace rows with a 6.5 Å measurement circled in an inset, matching the key's core feature, but it omits the key's stated "dark patches along them" and describes the inset as a bright-feature close-up rather than an FFT — a missing/altered detail rather than an outright contradiction.
